title: ONGC Profit More Than Doubles to ₹17,034 Crore as Surging Oil Prices Lift India's Top Explorer
excerpt: Brent crude's 45% year-on-year surge pushed ONGC's price realisation above $99 a barrel, delivering a standout quarter despite declining production.
body:
• ONGC's standalone net profit surged to ₹17,034 crore ($1.79 billion) in Q1 FY27, more than doubling from ₹8,024 crore a year earlier.
  • Crude oil price realisation jumped 50.4% to $99.45 per barrel, driven by Middle East supply disruptions that pushed average Brent prices up roughly 45% year-on-year.
  • Revenue from operations rose 45.2% to ₹46,460 crore, though standalone production slipped 3.4% as mature fields continued to decline.
  • Net profit margin improved sharply to 36.66% from 25.07%, the strongest quarterly margin in at least two years.

Oil and Natural Gas Corporation posted a blowout first quarter on Tuesday, with standalone profit more than doubling as surging crude prices offset a persistent decline in domestic production.

The Numbers

ONGC reported standalone net profit of ₹17,034 crore ($1.79 billion) for the three months ended June 30, compared with ₹8,024 crore in the year-ago quarter, according to a Reuters report citing the company's filings. Revenue from operations climbed 45.2% to ₹46,460 crore.

The result comfortably beat analyst expectations. The key driver was crude oil price realisation, which rose 50.4% to $99.45 per barrel from $66.13 a year earlier. Average global Brent crude prices surged roughly 45% year-on-year during the quarter as the prolonged Middle East conflict disrupted supply chains, pushed the market into deficit, and supported stronger upstream realisations globally.

"Upstream oil companies like ONGC are the clearest beneficiaries of a weakened rupee and surging crude prices, as the Middle East conflict pushed the market into deficit."

— Reuters analyst note

Margins at Multi-Year Highs

ONGC's net profit margin expanded to 36.66% from 25.07% a year ago — its strongest showing in at least two years. Total expenses rose a comparatively modest 13.4% to ₹25,474 crore, meaning revenue growth far outpaced cost inflation.

The company's shares have gained between 22% and 26% so far in 2026, riding the broader energy rally. Analysts at ICICI Securities have revised their FY27 and FY28 earnings estimates upward by 12% and 10% respectively, noting that current assumptions of $85-per-barrel realisations for FY27 may prove conservative if the oil market tightness persists.

Production Still Declining

The one persistent concern is production. Standalone crude output slipped 3.4% as several mature fields in ONGC's western offshore portfolio continued their natural decline. The company has flagged this trend for multiple quarters and is investing in new well drilling, workover interventions, and the long-awaited KG Basin deepwater development to arrest the slide.

Gas production was nearly flat. ONGC has been banking on its new-well gas allocation, which carries a premium price of $8.26 per mmbtu and contributed meaningfully to revenue growth last quarter.

What to Watch

The sustainability of these results depends almost entirely on where crude prices go from here. The Middle East supply disruption that powered Q1's numbers shows no sign of easing, but any diplomatic breakthrough or demand slowdown could compress realisations quickly. For now, investors are betting the cycle has further to run — ONGC's total dividend for FY26 hit a record ₹16,669 crore, and the Q1 result suggests FY27 payouts could match or exceed that.
nri_angle: ONGC is a bellwether for Indian energy and a staple of NRI investment portfolios; its results reflect both India's upstream fortunes and the global crude price cycle that affects fuel costs worldwide.
